claims.content: The Customer completes their transaction(s) for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for now, a shipping method, and a payment type.
Customer
The Customer is a registered user of the auction site and is signed in; guest checkout is not offered.
The Customer's account is active and is not closed or suspended; closed or suspended accounts cannot sign in.

The Customer's account is not in 'Review Status' or otherwise locked under the unpaid-winnings escalation policy; accounts with unresolved unpaid winnings older than 7 days or expired PayPal/Amazon orders are locked and can only be unlocked by a customer service representative.
The Customer is a returning winner: they have won one or more ended auctions and have unpaid won items listed in the system.
The Customer's default Method of Payment (MOP) on file is either PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The system has checked the Customer's registration data and identified the default payment method type as PayPal/Amazon, which routes the Customer to this interactive payment flow.
The Customer's unpaid orders won with PayPal or Amazon as the default MOP are in Hold status until payment is received.
The system displays a 'Winnings Alert' text bar in place of the normal promotional text bar because the Customer has unpaid winnings and a PayPal/Amazon default MOP.
In the 'Items I've Won' section, the Customer's unpaid items show a Payment Status of 'Not Paid' (in bold red), and that status links to the Returning Winners Payments page.
The Customer has been identified through one of the supported access paths: the 'Congratulations Winner!' email, a 'pay now' link, cookie identification, or by signing in.
The Customer has established billing and shipping addresses in the system.
The Customer has set a shipping preference (Standard or Expedited).
The Customer is completing payment within the 168-hour payment window; the unpaid order has not yet been cancelled for non-payment.

The use case is triggered when the Customer, after winning an auction with PayPal or Amazon Payments as the default Method of Payment, clicks the 'Not Paid' status link in the Payment Status column of the 'Items I've Won' section, the 'Winnings Alert' link (shown in place of the normal promotional text bar after sign-in), or the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email, navigating to the Returning Winners Payments page; the Customer may also reach that page via other provided links such as My Account or Bid History.

The system displays the 'Returning Winners Payments' page for the Customer. The page includes a personalized 'Welcome Back Winner!' message and a text paragraph explaining that the Customer must choose which items to pay for now, a shipping method, and a payment type, and that PayPal or Amazon is the Customer's default payment method.

The Customer reviews the listing of won but unpaid items, which includes Item #, Description, Auction Number, Amount owed, auction ending time, and a 'Pay Now' checkbox for each item; the formatting matches the 'My Bid History' page.
The Customer chooses which specific items to pay for now by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to the desired items.
The Customer selects a shipping method via radio buttons in the shipping options section: 'USPS Standard ($6.99)' or 'Expedited (5-day, add $5.00)'.
The Customer proceeds to the 'Checkout Options' section, which shows PayPal, Amazon Payments, and 'Checkout Later' logo/radio buttons, and selects PayPal or Amazon Payments as the payment type.

The system processes the selected checkout option: if the Customer clicked PayPal, it immediately takes the Customer to the PayPal-hosted checkout process; if the Customer clicked Amazon Payments, it immediately loads the Amazon Payments checkout widget on the same page, graying out the background and disabling other links.
The Customer completes payment for the selected winnings through the chosen PayPal or Amazon Payments checkout process.
The system returns the Customer to a 'Thank You' page, which uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The system sends a 'Shipping Confirmation' email through Responsys after the Customer completes payment for their winnings via PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The system sends another email shortly after payment completion confirming the Customer's order and shipping information.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer chooses the 'Checkout Later' button/radio button in the Checkout Options section instead of PayPal or Amazon Payments, the system immediately grays out the page and disables all links, then displays a 'No Problem!' DIV layer with the text: 'No Problem! You can come back to pay anytime within 7 days (exactly 168 hours) after winning your auction(s). Please remember though, any unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires. Lastly, please remember, to be fair to all of our auction participants, that bidding incurs an obligation on your part to pay when you win, per the Terms of Use Agreement.' The DIV layer provides a 'Return to Payments' link, which closes the DIV and re-enables page links, and a 'JTVauctions Homepage' link, which takes the Customer to the home page. The Checkout Later view does not include the global header or global footer.

Diverges from Step 7: If the Customer fails to complete payment for winnings won with PayPal or Amazon Payments within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, the system automatically cancels the unpaid orders and places the items into a 'hold' status.

Diverges from main_flow Step 7 (Customer completes payment for the selected winnings through the chosen PayPal or Amazon Payments checkout process): If the Customer fails to complete payment for winnings won with PayPal or Amazon Payments within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction's closing date/time, the system automatically cancels the unpaid orders, places the item(s) into 'Hold' status, counts the cancelled orders as churned auctions in reporting, and sends the Customer a notification that their account may be suspended (non-payment may also result in suspension and/or termination of bidding privileges). If the Customer has allowed the order(s) to remain unpaid until expiration, the system also locks the account into 'Review Status', which prevents sign-in and blocks access to checkout; only a Customer Service Representative can unlock the account, and the Customer cannot self-unlock by paying for the cancelled orders because those orders are already cancelled. Exit: the use case terminates for the cancelled orders; the Customer cannot resume this checkout flow for those items, and must contact Customer Service to unlock the account before being able to pay any remaining eligible unpaid items.

Recovery path after the Step 7 non-payment exception/lock: If the Customer whose account has been locked due to cancelled orders contacts Customer Service, a Customer Service Representative may unlock the account if the Customer has not failed to pay more than three times; upon contact, the Customer is reminded that winning incurs an obligation to pay. Exit: if the account is unlocked and the Customer still has unpaid winnings within the 168-hour payment window, the Customer may re-enter the use case at main_flow Step 1; otherwise the use case terminates.

Escalation path triggered by repeated non-payment: If the Customer becomes subject to the escalation policy (failing to pay more than three times in a twelve-month period, unless that count is less than 10% of total winnings), the Customer cannot bid again until a Customer Service Representative removes the account from 'Review Status'. Removal requires the Customer to update the account with a credit card, and PayPal or Amazon Payments may not be used again until the order cancel rate falls below 10%. Exit: the use case terminates; because this checkout flow requires PayPal or Amazon as the default MOP, the Customer cannot resume this flow until the Review Status is removed and the default payment method is eligible.
The Customer's payment for the selected won items has been successfully completed through PayPal or Amazon Payments.
The selected won items are no longer in an unpaid state: the bold red 'Not Paid' text and its link to the 'Returning Winner's Payments' page are removed from the Payment Status column.

For orders won with PayPal or Amazon Payments that were previously in Hold status, payment has been received within the 168-hour payment window; the Hold status is removed and the orders proceed to fulfillment instead of being cancelled.
The system generates an order for the Customer's paid winnings and ships the item(s) to the Customer.
Items won by the same bidder on the same calendar day are accumulated into a single order and submitted to JTV's Order Management System/OPL so they can be shipped together.
The Customer is returned to a 'Thank You' page that uses the global header and footer and includes a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The system sends a 'Shipping Confirmation' email to the Customer through Responsys after successful payment completion.
The system sends another email shortly after payment completion confirming the Customer's order and shipping information.

The shipped auction items include invoices/packing slips that are clearly distinct from other JTV products (different colored paper, different logo, different return policy printed on the invoice); different/distinctive invoices are used for each JTV auction site/storefront.
Auction winners do not receive BazaarVoice 'Please Review Your Item' email requests.
The payment platform is PCI compliant after successful checkout and payment completion.
